name: N-Acetylcysteine
summary: N-Acetylcysteine is a nootropic substance belonging to the Cysteine chemical class.

pharmacology.text: Acetylcysteine is a prodrug to L-cysteine, a precursor to the biologic antioxidant glutathione. Hence administration of acetylcysteine replenishes glutathione stores. Acetylcysteine also is a precursor to cystine, which in turn is a substrate for the cystine-glutamate antiporter on astrocytes; hence there is increasing glutamate release into the extracellular space.

uses.text: Acetylcysteine or N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is a mucolytic that is used to treat paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose and to loosen thick mucus in individuals with chronic bronchopulmonary disorders, such as pneumonia and bronchitis. It has been used to treat lactobezoar in infants. It is also sometimes used as a dietary supplement.

sideEffects.text: Common side effects include nausea and vomiting when taken orally.
